title: Binary search trees
overview: Implement a binary search tree with insert, contains, delete (all three cases), inorder, height and an O(1) length.
professor_notes: This is a pretty tough one, so keep time to work on it. Hints will be uploaded tonight.
review_checklist:
- [ ] `insert` adds new keys and ignores duplicates (size unchanged).
- [ ] `contains` returns True/False and works on an empty tree.
- [ ] `delete` handles a leaf, a node with one child, and a node with two children, including the root in each case.
- [ ] `delete` keeps the BST property everywhere after a two-children delete, with no duplicate keys left behind.
- [ ] `delete` of a missing key raises `KeyError` and leaves the size unchanged.
- [ ] `inorder` returns the keys in sorted order.
- [ ] `height` is -1 for an empty tree and 0 for a single node.
- [ ] `len(tree)` is O(1) and stays correct after inserts, duplicate inserts and deletes.
- [ ] Operations other than `inorder` and `height` are O(h).
- [ ] Keys are stored in nodes, not in a Python list or dict.
